# GateKit

> Tools for developing Baldur's Gate 3 mods: the game starts by itself, Lua reloads while it runs, and everything in it can be read and driven from code — by a person, a test or an AI agent. Experimental; built mostly by AI agents under human review.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what GateKit is and how to run it.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what an AI should know about this project before changing it; the map of the repository — architecture, where each thing lives, the rules. For an agent changing GateKit itself.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): from nothing to your own mod reloading live in the game.
- [Driving the game](docs/driving-the-game.md): connecting the MCP server and what its tools do — for an agent using GateKit.
- [Concepts](docs/concepts.md): how the host, the channel, the in-game mod and the extender fit together.

## Contracts (the exact reference)

- [Bridge protocol](docs/contracts/bridge-protocol.md): the file channel between the host and the game.
- [CLI](docs/contracts/cli.md): every command of `gatekit`, its settings and the files it touches.
- [MCP tools](docs/contracts/mcp.md): the tools an agent sees.
- [Lua API](docs/contracts/lua-api.md): what the in-game mod exposes as `GK.*`.

## What we worked out about the game

- [Measured facts](docs/facts.md): numbers measured on the game itself — start-up, memory, what the extender can and cannot do.
- [Levels](docs/levels.md): every level a test can start in cold, and what you get when it loads.
- [Rules an agent should know](docs/agent-rules.md): where Baldur's Gate 3 differs from D&D 5e, mechanics only.
- [Curiosities](docs/curiosities.md): what the game turned out to be doing — cut content, unfinished mechanics, oddities.

## Designs (planned, not built)

- [AI controllers](docs/design/ai-controllers.md): characters played by agents during combat — an AI companion, AI opponents, several minds at once.

## Optional

- [Weave](mods/Weave/README.md): in-game windows written like web pages.
- [GateKit mod](mods/GateKit/README.md): the bridge that runs inside the game.
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): language, naming and what is never committed.
- [Research](research/README.md): working material of the people and agents building GateKit — tools, journals and plans, not documentation.
